title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: A practical field guide to shared study, exercise, gallery, and outdoor spaces whose day-to-day uses are easy to miss on a standard campus visit.

cards.title: Bring the Group Without Booking a Room
cards.subtitle: First-come collaborative space in the library
cards.notes: Meet at the collaboratories when a group needs to work together without a reservation; arrive with a backup spot in case all ten are occupied.
cards.short_summary: Ten walk-in spaces provide an alternative to the library’s reservable study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The DiMenna-Nyselius Library provides ten collaboratory spaces that are first come, first served and cannot be reserved.
cards.source_title: Fairfield University Library — Reserve a Room
cards.access_notes: The room page is directed primarily to Fairfield students; normal library access policies apply.

cards.title: Use the Lab Between Scheduled Sessions
cards.subtitle: Drop-in study space with specialized workstations
cards.notes: Check whether a class or event is scheduled, then use the mobile workstations and screens for project work that benefits from a flexible setup.
cards.short_summary: The lab doubles as an interdisciplinary workspace when programming does not have priority.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fredrickson Family CAS Innovation Lab is available for drop-in study when no class or event is scheduled and includes mobile workstations and HDTV screens.
cards.source_title: Fairfield University Library — Reserve a Room
cards.access_notes: StagCard swipe controls room access, and scheduled classes or events take precedence.

cards.title: Pair Cardio With the Indoor Track
cards.subtitle: Machines and a four-lane loop on one level
cards.notes: Use the upper level when you want to alternate machine intervals with track laps; consult the live facility count before choosing a time.
cards.short_summary: The RecPlex groups its cardio inventory and indoor track on the top level.
cards.evidence_claim: The RecPlex top level contains 75 pieces of cardio equipment and a four-lane indoor track.
cards.access_notes: RecPlex entry requires an eligible membership card or StagCard; consult current facility rules.

cards.title: Find Strength Equipment on the Mezzanine
cards.subtitle: Selectorized, plate-loaded, and free-weight options
cards.notes: Head to the mezzanine for strength work, then adapt the session to available equipment and follow the facility’s posted use rules.
cards.short_summary: The mezzanine concentrates the RecPlex’s primary strength-training equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: The RecPlex identifies a mezzanine weight room with 35 selectorized and plate-loaded machines, while its facility gallery also documents free weights.
cards.access_notes: RecPlex entry requires an eligible membership card or StagCard; equipment rules apply.

cards.title: Confirm Open Swim Before Heading Over
cards.subtitle: An eight-lane pool inside the RecPlex
cards.notes: Call the reception desk or check the posted schedule before packing a swim bag; open swim is allowed only during designated periods.
cards.short_summary: The campus pool supports scheduled open swimming as well as varsity programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fairfield University Aquatics Center is an eight-lane, 25-meter pool, and the University instructs patrons to confirm the changing open-swim schedule.
cards.access_notes: Open swim is schedule-dependent and limited to eligible RecPlex users; pool rules apply.

cards.title: Look Beyond the Main Workout Floors
cards.subtitle: Lower-level rooms for scheduled fitness classes
cards.notes: Review the current class listing before going downstairs; the studios support formats such as yoga, Pilates, Zumba, and group exercise.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated lower-level studios host instructor-led movement sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The RecPlex lower level contains five multipurpose studios, including hardwood studios used for fitness and group-exercise classes.
cards.access_notes: RecPlex membership and the current class or facility schedule govern participation.

cards.title: Go Downstairs for the Museum Collection
cards.subtitle: Permanent displays and rotating exhibitions
cards.notes: Enter Bellarmine Hall during posted museum hours and head to the lower level; leave food, drinks, and backpacks outside the galleries.
cards.short_summary: The historic hall contains one of the University art museum’s two gallery locations.
cards.evidence_claim: The lower level of Bellarmine Hall houses permanent-collection displays and rotating Fairfield University Art Museum exhibitions.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free during posted museum hours; museum visitor policies and campus access rules apply.

cards.title: Check the Quick Center’s Exhibition Space
cards.subtitle: The museum’s larger special-exhibition gallery
cards.notes: Consult the current exhibition listing, then visit the Quick Center during posted gallery hours or before an eligible performance when access is offered.
cards.short_summary: Walsh Gallery gives temporary exhibitions a larger campus venue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fairfield University Art Museum identifies Walsh Gallery in the Quick Center as its larger special-exhibition space.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free during posted gallery hours; pre-performance access applies only when offered.

cards.title: Use the Museum Map as a Walking Prompt
cards.subtitle: Named artworks distributed across campus
cards.notes: Open the museum’s one-page map and choose a few labeled sculptures to connect; stay on appropriate campus paths and respect current access rules.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided map turns dispersed campus artworks into a flexible walking route.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fairfield University Art Museum publishes a campus map that identifies and illustrates named outdoor sculptures at multiple locations.
cards.source_title: Fairfield University Art Museum Outdoor Sculpture Map
cards.access_notes: The map does not promise unrestricted campus access; follow current visitor and pathway rules.

cards.title: Use the Business School Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Individual and group homework space near the library
cards.notes: Bring solo work or a small study group to the Dolan Centers, and use the charging stations or patio seating when those areas are available.
cards.short_summary: The business-school complex includes homework space alongside advising and academic centers.
cards.evidence_claim: Fairfield states that the Dolan Centers provide space for individual or group homework and that students have access to charging stations, patio seating, and comfortable work areas.
cards.source_title: Centers & Facilities | Charles F. Dolan School of Business
cards.access_notes: The page establishes student access but does not promise particular hours or unrestricted public entry.
